title: The universal form
hook: Arjuna gets what he asked for, and it's brighter than a thousand suns
carry: the whole universe lives in one god

segments.voice: Yesterday, divyam chakshuh: Arjuna asked to see, and got a divine eye. Your line was darshan: the sight of God is a gift. Today, he's shown.
screen: `DIVYAM CHAKSHUH — DARSHAN: THE SIGHT OF GOD IS A GIFT.`

segments.voice: One sun at noon is already too bright to look at. Add a second beside it. Then ten. Then a hundred. Then a thousand, all at once, all blazing. You can't look at it. You can't look away. That's the measure the Gita reaches for when Arjuna, with his new divine eye, finally sees what he asked to see. Sanjaya, telling it, has no ordinary comparison left, so he stacks up suns.
screen: `ONE SUN AT NOON.` → `THEN A THOUSAND, AT ONCE.` → `TOO BRIGHT TO LOOK AT.`

segments.voice: Sanjaya tells it. Having spoken, the great lord of yoga showed Arjuna his supreme form. Many mouths and eyes, many wonders, divine ornaments, divine weapons raised. Faces turned in every direction. Verse twelve: if the light of a thousand suns were to blaze up in the sky all at once, it might be like the splendor of that great being. Verse thirteen: there, in the body of the god of gods, Arjuna saw the whole universe, divided in countless ways, gathered as one. He bows his head, joins his palms, and speaks. At first it's wonder. I see all the gods in your body, and all kinds of beings. Brahma on his lotus, the sages, the divine serpents. I see you everywhere, with countless arms and eyes. No end, no middle, no beginning. The sun and moon are your eyes. Then it turns. The mouths have fangs. The worlds are trembling, and so am I. Arjuna sees the warriors of both armies, the men he's about to fight, his own teachers and great-uncle among them, rushing into those mouths like rivers running into the ocean, like moths flying into a flame. It's beautiful and it's terrifying, and the Gita doesn't soften either. Verse thirty-one: tell me, who are you, in this fierce form? I bow to you. Be gracious. I want to understand you; I don't know what you're doing. That's the vishvarupa, the universal form, and it carries one of Hinduism's biggest teachings: God isn't one being among many, off somewhere. Every god, every star, every life and every ending is held inside one God. It's why so many Hindus bow to the divine in everything, including the parts that frighten us.
screen: `FACES IN EVERY DIRECTION.` · `THE LIGHT OF A THOUSAND SUNS.` · `NO END, NO MIDDLE, NO BEGINNING.` · `LIKE MOTHS INTO A FLAME.` · then, large: `WHO ARE YOU?`

segments.voice: Feel your own body breathing, then widen: the room, the street, the city, the whole country at this hour, people waking and sleeping, being born and dying, then the earth turning in sunlight. Let it be too big to hold, and notice what that feels like: wonder, fear, or both. Then, if you pray, end as Arjuna did, palms joined, with a small bow; if not, simply come back to one breath.
Vishvarupa. The universal form: the whole universe seen at once in God's body, brighter than a thousand suns, wonderful and terrible.
Your line: the whole universe lives in one God. Arjuna asked to see, and he saw. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: The vishvarupa, the universal form of Gita chapter eleven, is painted, sculpted and staged across Hindu art and temple traditions, and many devotees read the chapter with awe as the Gita's great vision.

original.note: Sanskrit: vishvarupa, the universal form; vishva (all, the universe) + rupa (form).

trapdoor: what you thought: seeing God would be peaceful.
what it means: the universal form shows everything at once, creation and destruction, brighter than a thousand suns, and it overwhelms Arjuna.
what a scholar hears: 11.12's 'divi surya-sahasrasya' gave Robert Jungk's 1956 book its title; the chapter is called vishvarupa-darshana yoga, the yoga of seeing the universal form.
recall: the king of secrets, the highest one

vishvarupa.meaning: the universal form: the whole universe seen in God's body

Sanjaya.meaning: the narrator, telling the battle to the blind king

Brahma.meaning: the creator god, seen seated on his lotus

Gita.meaning: the Bhagavad Gita, Krishna's teaching to Arjuna on the battlefield

notes: All verses paraphrased; Arnold 1885 (The Song Celestial) has a public-domain rendering of 11.12, but it isn't quoted because its exact wording couldn't be confirmed.
Jungk's book: German 'Heller als tausend Sonnen' (1956), English 1958. The voice says 'in 1956 a book... took its title'; confirm.
Check the vision's details: Brahma on the lotus (11.15), no end/middle/beginning (11.16), sun and moon as eyes (11.19), rivers into the ocean and moths into flame (11.28–29).
